name: What is the best garage conversion layout for rental income?

mainEntity.name: Should a garage ADU be designed as a studio, one-bedroom, or two-bedroom if the goal is rental value in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Should a garage ADU be designed as a studio, one-bedroom, or two-bedroom if the goal is rental value in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: The highest-performing layout is not always the largest one. For many Los Angeles-area garages, a one-bedroom plan provides a strong balance between construction cost and rental appeal because it offers enough privacy for tenants without overly compressing the layout. Studios can work well in smaller garages or for shorter-term occupancy, while a two-bedroom layout may only make sense if the garage is unusually large or the design can preserve good circulation and storage. The best rental layout should also consider natural light, kitchen size, bathroom quality, and privacy from the main house. Homeowners should think about who the likely renter is and what features matter most in that market. A flexible, well-lit, quiet one-bedroom often competes better than a cramped two-bedroom. The smartest decision is usually the one that maximizes comfort per square foot rather than trying to force too much program into the garage shell.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best rental layout depends on lot size, market demand, and the garage’s footprint, but a one-bedroom often offers a strong balance of livability and rent potential. Studios can fit smaller garages, while two-bedroom layouts are usually harder to achieve without a larger structure.
